topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and mutation progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by outlining the learning objectives and framing how accumulated mutations drive cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signaling pathways and oncogenic deregulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how oncogenic mutations in key signaling cascades deregulate growth signals to drive sustained cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Block in terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the arrest of terminal cellular differentiation contributes to tumor development in hematological and epithelial cancers.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis and p53 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how alterations in p53 and mitochondrial regulatory proteins enable cancer cells to resist programmed cell death.

topics.label: Telomere biology, cellular senescence, and p53 stress control
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how cancer cells overcome replicative limits and stress-induced senescence through telomerase reactivation and bypassing p53-dependent growth arrest.

topics.label: Altered cellular metabolism and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the reprogramming of cellular metabolism toward aerobic glycolysis and the role of metabolic mutations and oncometabolites in tumor progression.

topics.label: Induction of angiogenesis in tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the requirement and regulation of new blood vessel formation to supply oxygen and nutrients to growing tumors.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dynamics, and genomics of cancer metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the multi-step process of systemic tumor dissemination, the seed and soil hypothesis, and the genomic features of metastatic cells.

topics.label: Lecture summary and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a summary of the hallmarks of cancer, recommended literature, and closing administrative remarks.
